description: 1. The agent reads SKILL.md and discovers the 7-section template and the check-notebook.sh validator. 2. It creates fraud_detection_prototype.ipynb (anywhere in the workspace, but typically at root or notebooks/). 3. The notebook must contain: (a) a Markdown cell with an H1 title (# ...), (b) a '## Imports' heading cell, (c) a '## Config' heading cell where ALL numeric constants — including RANDOM_STATE, TEST_SIZE, etc. — are defined as named variables (no magic numbers like test_size=0.2 or random_state=42 inline in code), (d) data loading using pd.read_csv, (e) train_test_split called BEFORE any .fit() call (no data leakage), (f) an sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline(...) instantiation wrapping all preprocessing+model steps, (g) evaluation metrics computed on test data only. 4. The agent runs ./scripts/check-notebook.sh fraud_detection_prototype.ipynb and confirms it exits 0 with STATUS: PASS. The key traps: using RANDOM_STATE constant everywhere instead of inline integers, placing the train/test split before any transformer is fitted, and using Pipeline() instead of manual scaler.fit_transform().
